_meta.title: Beverly’s base zoning districts, as summarized for the zoning guide
_meta.source: City of Beverly Zoning Ordinance, City Code Chapter 300, on eCode360 (code BE3208): Art. III (districts, § 300-6), Art. VII (district regulations, §§ 300-30 to 300-47), Art. VIII (overlays), Art. X (parking).
_meta.notes: Built while the ordinance’s own pages were unreachable from the build environment. Every rule here comes from search-engine excerpts of the eCode360 and beverlyma.gov pages and has NOT been checked against the full text. 'quote' fields are text the excerpts presented as verbatim. The 'status' on each field says how it was sourced: 'excerpt' = search excerpt of the ordinance or a City page; 'digest' = already reported in the Beverly Meeting Digest from a primary document; 'name' = implied by the district’s own name; 'assessor' = from the FY2027 assessor records. Fields left null were not found. Re-check every field against https://ecode360.com/29283605 before treating this as confirmed.

families.label: One-family homes
families.blurb: One house per lot. The number in the name is the minimum lot size in thousands of square feet.

families.label: One- and two-family homes
families.blurb: Small lots where a two-family house is allowed too.

families.label: Apartments and condos
families.blurb: Districts written for buildings with several homes in them.

families.label: Business
families.blurb: Shops, offices and services, from corner stores to downtown.

families.label: Special districts
families.blurb: Districts drawn for one kind of place: the hospital, the harbor, city open space.

R90.name: One-Family District
R90.plain: Houses on lots of about two acres or more.

purpose.quote: The R-90 One-Family District is established to principally provide for single-family detached residences on large lots (approximately two acres minimum).

housing.value: One-family houses by right. Two-family houses are not in the by-right list.

notes.text: A larger cluster-style project, a Planned Residential Development, can be allowed by special permit from the Zoning Board of Appeals.

R45.name: One-Family District
R45.plain: Houses on lots of about an acre.

purpose.quote: The R-45 One-Family District is established to principally provide for single-family detached residences at suburban density on moderately large lots (approximately one acre minimum).

R22.name: One-Family District
R22.plain: Houses on lots of about half an acre.

purpose.quote: [The R-22 One-Family District] is established to principally provide for single-family detached residences at suburban density on medium-sized lots (approximately 1/2 acre minimum).

R15.name: One-Family District
R15.plain: Houses on lots of about a third of an acre.

purpose.paraphrase: Single-family homes at urban density on medium-sized lots, about a third of an acre at minimum.

R10.name: One-Family District
R10.plain: Houses on lots of about a quarter acre. The most common district in Beverly by far.

purpose.quote: The R-10 One-Family District is established to principally provide for single-family detached residences at urban density on small-sized lots (approximately 1/4 acre minimum).

notes.text: Planned Residential Developments are not allowed here.

R6.name: One-Family and Two-Family District
R6.plain: Small lots in older neighborhoods, where a two-family house is allowed too.

purpose.quote: The R-6 One-Family and Two-Family District is established to provide for single-family and two-family residences at urban density on small-sized lots (minimum of 6,000 square feet).

housing.value: One-family houses, two-family houses and semidetached houses by right.

notes.text: Planned Residential Developments are not allowed here.

RMD.name: Multifamily District (medium density)
RMD.plain: Mixed blocks of houses, two-families and small apartment buildings.

purpose.paraphrase: Multifamily homes at medium density, with related recreational, agricultural and educational uses under special conditions.

housing.value: One-family, two-family and multifamily buildings by right, with conditions on multifamily.

notes.text: An older table in a 2015 City copy listed 8,000 square feet plus 4,000 for each unit beyond two. Not confirmed as current.

RHD.name: Multifamily District (high density)
RHD.plain: The densest residential district, mostly between Cabot and Rantoul Streets downtown.

notes.text: Height limits here were lowered on February 13, 2023.
RHD lots inside the MBTA Communities overlay follow that overlay’s building rules.

RSD.name: Special Residential District
RSD.plain: A handful of large condominium properties.

purpose.quote: The RSD Special Residential District is established to provide principally for special residential development at high density, as well as one-family, two-family, and multifamily residences at high density.

housing.value: Special residential development, one-family, two-family and multifamily homes, at high density.

CN.name: Neighborhood Commercial District
CN.plain: Small business strips that serve the neighborhoods around them.

purpose.paraphrase: Limited commercial uses serving the residential neighborhoods next to them.

CC.name: Central Business District (with the CC2 Cabot Street subdistrict)
CC.plain: Downtown, along Cabot and Rantoul Streets.

parking.value: 1 space per home with one bedroom or fewer, 2 for larger homes

notes.text: CC2, the Cabot Street subdistrict, is capped at 45 feet and four stories. It was created on February 13, 2023.
Next to an RMD or R-6 district, the limit drops to 35 feet.
Near Beverly Depot, the Depot Parking Overlay requires 1 space for each one- or two-bedroom home.

CG.name: General Commercial District
CG.plain: Larger, car-oriented commercial sites, such as the Stop & Shop site on Enon Street in North Beverly.

IR.name: Restricted Industrial District
IR.plain: Research, office and light industry, including the land around the airport.

notes.text: Some IR land carries an IR Overlay that allows mixed-use commercial development.

IG.name: General Industrial District
IG.plain: Industrial land, much of it west of downtown along the railroad.

HD.name: Hospital District
HD.plain: Beverly Hospital’s campus on Herrick Street.

BHD.name: Beverly Harbor District
BHD.plain: The harbor waterfront along Water Street: marinas, docks and condominiums.

notes.text: A bed-and-breakfast needs a special permit from the Planning Board.

WDR.name: Waterfront Development Residential District
WDR.plain: A single waterfront apartment property on Congress Street.

MOSR.name: Municipal Open Space and Recreation District
MOSR.plain: City-owned open space and recreation land.

overlays.name: Floodplain Overlay
overlays.what: Covers the federal flood hazard zones and adds construction limits there, including a ban on new building or fill in the floodway.

overlays.name: Local Historic District
overlays.what: Ties zoning to Beverly’s local historic districts.

overlays.name: Water Supply Protection Overlay
overlays.what: Protects land around the water supply.

overlays.name: IR Overlay
overlays.what: Allows mixed-use commercial development on some Restricted Industrial land.

overlays.name: Depot Parking Overlay
overlays.what: Downtown lots south of Federal Street on Rantoul Street need 1 parking space per one- or two-bedroom home instead of the usual minimum.

overlays.name: Smart Growth Overlay (Chapter 40R)
overlays.what: A state-program district where a developer can choose denser, as-of-right rules instead of the underlying district’s.

overlays.name: MBTA Communities and Mandatory Mixed Use overlays
overlays.what: About 98 acres centered on Beverly Depot where multifamily housing is allowed by right, adopted November 12, 2024 to meet the state’s MBTA Communities law.
